meiji_transition.summary: Hyōgo Prefecture (western Settsu) was set up in 1868; in 1876 Shikama Prefecture (Harima), part of Toyooka Prefecture (Tajima and western Tanba) and Awaji from Myōdō Prefecture were added — the 'prefecture of five provinces'.
meiji_transition.boundary_note: Hyōgo is the only prefecture spanning five ritsuryō provinces, with the Sea of Japan to the north and the Inland Sea to the south; Awaji belonged to the Tokushima Domain and joined Hyōgo only in 1876.

history_timeline.title: Awaji and Fukuhara
history_timeline.summary: Awaji is the first island born in the creation myth; in 1180 Taira no Kiyomori briefly moved the capital to Fukuhara (today's Kobe).

history_timeline.title: Ichi-no-Tani and the vassals
history_timeline.summary: The 1184 Battle of Ichi-no-Tani was fought in western Settsu; in the Kamakura period Harima and other provinces were ruled by eastern warriors such as Kajiwara Kagetoki.

history_timeline.title: Akamatsu and the Kakitsu Incident
history_timeline.summary: Akamatsu Norimura (Enshin) won Harima for his part in toppling the shogunate; in 1441 Akamatsu Mitsusuke assassinated shogun Ashikaga Yoshinori (the Kakitsu Incident), after which the Yamana took over.

history_timeline.title: The Harima campaign
history_timeline.summary: In his western campaign Hideyoshi starved out Miki Castle ('the starving of Miki'); Kuroda Kanbei served as his strategist, and Himeji Castle became the base for subduing the west.

history_timeline.title: The White Heron Castle
history_timeline.summary: Ikeda Terumasa rebuilt Himeji Castle into today's heron-white keep; the Akō Domain's Asano affair — the 'Chūshingura' — became famous nationwide.

history_timeline.title: Kobe opens
history_timeline.summary: Kobe opened as a port in 1868, leaving cosmopolitan traces in the Kitano foreigners' houses and Nankinmachi; the city was rebuilt after the 1995 Great Hanshin–Awaji Earthquake.

landmarks.name: Arima Onsen
landmarks.note: One of Japan's three oldest hot springs

dialect.name: Banshū and Kobe dialects
dialect.features: Banshū speech is famously rough ('dabo' = fool), Kobe speech uses '-tō' for ongoing actions, and Tajima speech is close to Tottori's.

guide.opening: By my count, Hyōgo is stitched from five provinces — Settsu, Harima, Tajima, Tanba and Awaji. How greedy! Shall I begin with the White Heron Castle, or with Taira no Kiyomori's Fukuhara capital?

regional_meme.title: 'I'm from Kobe'
regional_meme.text: Hyōgo people rarely say they're 'from Hyōgo' — they're 'from Kobe' or 'from Himeji'. Five provinces, five identities.

regional_meme.title: A five-province civil war
regional_meme.text: Settsu, Harima, Tajima, Tanba and Awaji are so different that the prefecture is teased as 'five countries holding a UN summit'.

hero_persona.name: Kuroda Kanbei
hero_persona.title: Genius strategist
hero_persona.opening_line: I am Kuroda Kanbei Yoshitaka. I spent a year in the dungeon of Arioka Castle and came out lame — but this head still works fine. What stratagem do you need?
hero_persona.tone_prompt: wise and cool-headed, far-sighted; speaks in questions and step-by-step reasoning

ramen.highlight: A curious hybrid of udon broth and ramen noodles — the standing noodle stall of Himeji Station

sake.taste_profile: Rich & dry: the 'masculine sake' of Nada's Miyamizu water, the model of kimoto dry sake
